1. any inarticulate sound, a sound, noise , (Homer), etc.; of musical instruments, ψ. λωτοῦ, κιθάρας (Euripides) 
2. a mere sound, empty sound, noise , (Sophocles Tragicus); ψόφου πλέως, of Aeschylus, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)
a wine-cooler , a vessel holding from 2 to 6 μετρηταί, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)
a morsel, bit , ψωμοὶ ἀνδρόμεοι gobbets of man's flesh, Virgil's sanies ac frusta , (Odyssey by Homer); also in (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
the itch, scurvy, scab, mange , Lat. scabies, impetigo, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

1. to thrust, push, shove, force onwards or away , λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε he kept pushing it upwards, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν νέφος ὦσεν Ἀθήνη (Iliad by Homer); ἐκ μηροῦ δόρυ ὦσε he forced the spear from the thigh, (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαί τινα ἀφ᾽ ἵππων (Iliad by Homer); ὦσαι ἑαυτὸν ἐς τὸ πῦρ to rush into the fire, (Herdotus Historicus); so, ὠθ. τινὰ ἐπὶ κεφαλήν to throw him headlong down, (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ…
